| | 3. Verifies availability of allotment based on the appropriate RAOD. If allotment is not available, returns the documents to the Accounting Office staff. |
| | 4. Prepares the Obligation Request and Status (ORS) in two copies. |
| | 5. If allotment is available, assigns number on the ORS/ Budget Utilization Request and Status (BURS) based on the Control Logbook maintained for the purpose. Records the amount obligated based on the ORS in the ‘Obligation’column of the RAOD. |
| | 6. Reviews the ORS and SDs. If in order, signs the certification in Section B of the ORS. |
7. Forwards the ORS and SDs to the Accounting Office for processing of the claim. Retains original copy of the ORS for maintenance/monitoring of obligation status.
Accounting Staff-3 8. Receives Copies of SDs and Copies 2-3 of ORS/BURS from the Budget Office. Checks completeness of SDs based on the checklist. Note – Copy 1 of the ORS/BURS shall be retained by the Budget Office, which shall serve as the subsidiary ledger of obligations.

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or teh Freedom of Information Policy

0 – offers the highest price among the external providers
1 – offers a competitive or relatively lower price than the other external providers
2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers
3.1.3.3 Delivery Lead Time (10%)
0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.3.4 Availability/Capacity (10%)
0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
1 – can supply the average requirements of the company
2 – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall not be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations adn laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. 0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company

3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with the Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 The system of rewards and recognition shall be designed to encourage creativity, innovativeness, efficiency, integrity and productivity in the public service by recognizing and rewarding officials and employees individually or in groups for their suggestions, inventions, superior accomplishments and other personal efforts which contribute to the efficiency, economy or other improvement in government operations, or for other extraordinary acts or services in the public interest.
3.3 The Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) shall adhere to the principle of providing incentives and awards based on performance, innovative ideas and exemplary behavior.
3.4 The PRAISE shall provide both monetary and non-monetary awards and incentives to recognize, acknowledge and reward productive, creative, innovative and ethical behavior of employees through formal and informal mode.
3.5 A portion of the Human Resource Office funds shall be allocated for the PRAISE and incorporated in the LNU Annual Work and Financial Plan and Budget.

3.4 The PRAISE shall provide both monetary and non-monetary awards and incentives to recognize, acknowledge and reward productive, creative, innovative and ethical behavior of employees through formal and informal mode.

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

4.1 For Light Offenses
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard/ Faculty/Personnel/ | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Student | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of the Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD. |
| Student | 3. Fills out a Permit to Enter the Campus/Attend Class if the offense is non-wearing of school ID because it was left at home or lost. |
| Student | 4. Fills out an Admission Slip if referred to the Office of the VPSD due to accumulated absences |
| Student | 5. Reports to the guidance counselor with the Disciplinary Action Slip with an attached promissory letter for the guidance counselor’s signature and admonition. |
| Guidance Counselor | 6. Gives admonition/Reminds student of the specific rule he/she Violated and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
| OSD Staff | 7. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Student | 8. Reports to the VPSD to clear his/her violation. |
| VPSD | 9. Evaluates the case, admonish the student, and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
4.2 For Serious and Very Serious Offenses:
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD |
| OSD Staff | 3. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Preliminary Hearing Committee (PHC) | 4. Determines if such a complaint or report is sufficient to warrant a formal investigation. In cases where the complaint or report is found sufficient, formal charges shall be filed and served upon the respondent and his/her parent or guardian. |
| Student Respondent | 5. Answers in writing within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the charges. If there is no reply, a formal investigation shall beheld. |
| Chair of the Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 6. Notifies the student as well as his/her parents/guardians regarding the date and venue of the formal hearing. |
| Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 7. Renders its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. |
| Student | 8. May appeal to the University President if the sanction is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, the appeal shall be elevated to the Board of Regents (BOR) for review. |
| University President | 9. Reviews the case and renders his/her decision if the decision is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, he/she elevates the case to the Board of Regents (BOR). |
| Board of Regents | 10. Reviews the decision of the SDC and renders final judgment. |

3.14.1 Teh University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system

1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.2 Any request for information shall be governed by Executive Order No. 02, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information.

new_text:
3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 02, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information.
3.3 Accounts Receivable should be collected in a timely manner.
3.4 Credentials and official records of Undergraduate students will not be released if they still have unpaid school fees prior to the implementation of the Free Higher Education.
3.5 Credentials and official records of ILS/PLC and Masters/Doctoral students will only be released upon settlement of all their assessed school fees.
3.6 Accounts Receivable that are outstanding for more than 365 days or 1 year are considered past due already.
3.7 Demand Letters should be sent to the debtors for those past due accounts.

old_text:
3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company
10-15 pts – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company

The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:

1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment ,or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)

In no case shall teh flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record ,which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure adn incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 Teh University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, adn 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.

4.1 Recording of Collections and Deposits
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Receives original of Report of Collection and Deposits (RCD) with Copy 2 of the Official Receipts (ORs) and validated Deposit Slips (DSs) from the Cash Management Office. |
| | 2. Records receipt in the logbook maintained for the purpose and forwards the same to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) for review and preparation of the Journal Entry Voucher (JEV). |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 3. Based on the RCD, prepares JEV using the eNGAS system. |
| Accountant | 4. Reviews and approves the JEV using the eNGAS system. The JEV will be automatically reflected in the General Journal and posted in the Ledger. |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 5. Prints the JEV in two copies and signs “Prepared by” portion of the JEV. |
| | 6. Forwards the JEV to the University Accountant for signature. |
| Accountant | 7. Signs “Certified Correct by” portion of the JEV, and forwards it back to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) afterwards. |
4.2 Recording of Disbursements made through check
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Receives copies of Report of Checks Issued (RCI) with Copy 2 of the Check, Disbursement Vouchers (DVs), Obligation Request and Status (ORS) and other supporting documents (SDs) from the Cash Management Office. |
| | 2. Forwards the documents to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) for JEV preparation. |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 3. Examines DVs and checks against RCI. Verifies if the serial number of all checks drawn whether released or unreleased, including spoiled and cancelled ones, are all accounted for. |
| | 4. Prepares JEV using the eNGAS system. Forwards the RCI, Check, DVs, ORS, and other SDs to the Accountant. |
4.3 Recording of Liquidation/ Disbursements made out of Advances for Payroll
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Records the receipt of the Report of Cash Disbursements (RCDisb) in the logbook, indicates “Received” and signs on all copies, forwards RCDisb to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) for JEV preparation, and returns copy 2 to the Cash Management Office. |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 2. Verifies completeness of data in the RCDisb as against the SDs received. Prepares JEV using the eNGAS system. Forwards the RCDisb to the University Accountant. |
| Accountant | 3. Reviews correctness of the journal entries and approves the JEV using the eNGAS system. The JEV will be automatically reflected in the General Journal and posted in the Ledger. |
| | 4. Returns the RCDisb to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff). |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 5. Prints the JEV in two copies and signs “Prepared by” portion of the JEV. Forwards the JEV to the Accountant for signature. |
| Accountant | 6. Signs “Certified Correct by” portion of the JEV, and forwards it back to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) afterwards. |
4.4 Recording of Liquidation/ Disbursements made out of Advances to Officers and Employees
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 1. Prepares JEV based on the Liquidation Report (LR) and SDs received using the eNGAS system. Forwards the LR and SDs to the Accountant. |
4.5 Recording of Liquidation/ Disbursements made out of Advances to Special Disbursing Officer
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Checks completeness of SDs. If complete, acknowledges receipt of RCDisb, returns copy 2 to the Accountable/ Special Disbursing Officer and records the same in the logbook. Otherwise, returns the documents to the Accountable/ Special Disbursing Officer |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 2. Verifies completeness and propriety of RCDisb and SDs. If complete and proper, prepares JEV using the eNGAS system. Otherwise, informs the Accountable/ Special Disbursing Officer of the deficiencies. Forwards RCDisb and SDs to the University Accountant. |
| Accountant | 3. Reviews correctness of the journal entries and approves the JEV using the eNGAS system. The JEV will be automatically reflected in the General Journal and posted in the Ledger. |
| | 4. Returns the RCDisb and SDs to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff). |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 5. Prints the JEV in two copies and signs “Prepared by” portion of the JEV. Forwards the JEV to the Accountant for signature. |
| Accountant | 6. Signs “Certified Correct by” portion of the JEV, and forwards it back to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) afterwards. |
4.6 Recording of Disbursements made through List of Due and Demandable Accounts Payable-Advice to Debit Account (LDDAP-ADA)
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Receives Report of Advice to Debit Account Issued (RADAI) from the Cash Management Office supported with Summary List of Issued and Invalidated ADA Entries (SLIIAE), validated LDDAP-ADA, DVs, and SDs. |
| Accounting Staff-6 | 2. Examines DVs and copies of validated LDDAP-ADA against RADAI. Verifies if the serial numbers of all the LDDAP-ADA issued are all accounted for. |
| | 3. Prepares JEV using the eNGAS system. Forwards the RADAI, SLIIAE, validated LDDAP-ADA, DVs, and SDs to the Accountant. |
| Accountant | 4. Reviews correctness of the journal entries and approves the JEV using the eNGAS system. The JEV will be automatically reflected in the General Journal and posted in the Ledger. |
| | 5. Returns the RADAI, SLIIAE, validated LDDAP-ADA, DVs, and SDs to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff). |
| Accounting Staff-6 | 6. Prints the JEV in two copies and signs “Prepared by” portion of the JEV. Forwards the JEV to the Accountant for signature. |
| Accountant | 7. Signs “Certified Correct by” portion of the JEV, and forwards it back to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) afterwards. |
4.7 Recording of Disbursements made through Tax Remittance Advice (TRA)
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-5 | 1. Upon receipt from the University President/ Authorized Official of the approved Electronic Tax Remittance Advice (eTRA), Summary of Taxes Withheld (SWT) and required tax returns (BIR Form Nos. 1600, 1601C, 0619E or 1601EQ), forwards the same to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff) for the preparation of JEV. |
| Accounting Staff-6 | 2. Prepares JEV using the eNGAS system for the constructive receipt of Notice of Cash Allocation (NCA) for TRA and remittance of all taxes withheld thru TRA. Forwards the eTRA, SWT and tax returns to the Accountant. |
| Accountant | 3. Reviews correctness of the journal entries and approves the JEV using the eNGAS system. The JEV will be automatically |
4.8 Submission of Financial Reports to the Commission on Audit (COA)
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 1. Prints the Trial Balances (TBs), Supporting Schedules (SSs), and separate and consolidated Financial Statements (FSs) for all fund categories based on the timing of reporting per Section 3.2 above. |
| | 2. Forwards the TBs, SSs, and FSs to the Accountant for signature. |
| Accountant | 3. Signs the TBs, SSs, and FSs. |
| | 4. Returns the TBs, SSs, and FSs to the Bookkeeper (Accounting Staff). |
| Accounting Staff-1 or 6 | 5. Submit the TBs, SSs, and FSs to COA. A copy of the Consolidated Annual Financial Statements of the University will also be given to the University President, CAO Finance, and VP for Administration and Finance. |

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN ,and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

| Student | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of the Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD. |
| Student | 3. Fills out a Permit to Enter the Campus/Attend Class if the offense is non-wearing of school ID because it was left at home or lost. |
| Student | 4. Fills out an Admission Slip if referred to the Office of the VPSD due to accumulated absences |
| Student | 5. Reports to the guidance counselor with the Disciplinary Action Slip with an attached promissory letter for the guidance counselor’s signature and admonition. |
| Guidance Counselor | 6. Gives admonition/Reminds student of the specific rule he/she Violated and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
| OSD Staff | 7. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Student | 8. Reports to the VPSD to clear his/her violation. |
| VPSD | 9. Evaluates the case, admonish the student, and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |

| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |

| OSD Staff | 3. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |

| Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 7. Renders its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. |
| Student | 8. May appeal to the University President if the sanction is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, the appeal shall be elevated to the Board of Regents (BOR) for review. |
| University President | 9. Reviews the case and renders his/her decision if the decision is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, he/she elevates the case to the Board of Regents (BOR). |
| Board of Regents | 10. Reviews the decision of the SDC and renders final judgment. |

3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company
10-15 pts – can supply the maximum requirements of the company
3.1.3 Evaluation summary shall be one of the following:
| REGULAR | 75-100 | 50-74 | 15-49 | 0-14 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Retain supplier | Retain supplier, point out weakness | Discretion of ED/CD | Suspend business |
| NEW | 30-50 | 20-29 | 10-19 | 0-9 |
| | Can start business | Can start business, ask to improve | Discretion of ED/CD | No business |

| Chair of the Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 6. Notifies the student as well as his/her parents/guardians regarding the date and venue of the formal hearing. |
| Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 7. Renders its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. |

| University President | 9. Reviews the case and renders his/her decision if the decision is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, he/she elevates the case to the Board of Regents (BOR). |
| Board of Regents | 10. Reviews the decision of the SDC and renders final judgment. |

2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers

0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented ,the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service ,without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company
10-15 pts – can supply the maximum requirements of the company
3.1.3 Evaluation summary shall be one of the following:
| REGULAR | 75-100 | 50-74 | 15-49 | 0-14 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Retain supplier | Retain supplier, point out weakness | Discretion of ED/CD | Suspend business |
| NEW | 30-50 | 20-29 | 10-19 | 0-9 |
| | Can start business | Can start business, ask to improve | Discretion of ED/CD | No business |

3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company
10-15 pts – can supply the maximum requirements of the company
3.1.3 Evaluation summary shall be one of the following:
| REGULAR | 75-100 | 50-74 | 15-49 | 0-14 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Retain supplier | Retain supplier, point out weakness | Discretion of ED/CD | Suspend business |
| NEW | 30-50 | 20-29 | 10-19 | 0-9 |
| | Can start business | Can start business, ask to improve | Discretion of ED/CD | No business |

The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure and incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. Teh certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

old_text:
3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with the Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 The system of rewards and recognition shall be designed to encourage creativity, innovativeness, efficiency, integrity and productivity in the public service by recognizing and rewarding officials and employees individually or in groups for their suggestions, inventions, superior accomplishments and other personal efforts which contribute to the efficiency, economy or other improvement in government operations, or for other extraordinary acts or services in the public interest.
3.3 The Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) shall adhere to the principle of providing incentives and awards based on performance, innovative ideas and exemplary behavior.
3.4 The PRAISE shall provide both monetary and non-monetary awards and incentives to recognize, acknowledge and reward productive, creative, innovative and ethical behavior of employees through formal and informal mode.
3.5 A portion of the Human Resource Office funds shall be allocated for the PRAISE and incorporated in the LNU Annual Work and Financial Plan and Budget.
