0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.3.4 Availability/Capacity (10%)
0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
1 – can supply the average requirements of the company
2 – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with the Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 The LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is in line with the guidelines in the establishment and implementation of Agency enunciated under CSC Resolution No. 1200481 MC No. 6, s. 2012,
3.3 The LNU SPMS adheres to the principle of performance-based security of tenure. It provides motivation and basis for incentives to performers and applies sanctions to nonperformers.
3.4 The LNU SPMS operates on shared commitments and objective measures of performance results. Performance targets and standards or measures of results are planned and agreed upon by management, supervisors and employees.
3.5 The LNU SPMS enhances productivity by using performance targets and standards attuned to organizational goals and mandate.
3.6 The LNU SPMS promotes transparency and provides mechanism for appeals and resolution of conflicts and/or disagreements.
3.7 Pursuant to the Section 7.4 of Memorandum Circular (MC) No. 2013-01 of the Inter Agency Task Force on the Harmonization of the National Government Performance Monitoring, Information and Reporting Systems as per Administrative Order No. 25, s. 2011, the CSC approved SPMS of the Leyte Normal University will be used in evaluating office and individual performance.
3.8 The ratings in all SPMS forms shall follow the following scales:
A. Quality
| Rating | Accuracy | Customer Feedback | Completeness of Documents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | No revision | 4.5 – 5.0 | Complete |
| 4 | Minor revision | 3.5 – 4.4 | Lacking 1 |
| 3 | Major revision | 3.0 – 3.4 | Lacking 2-3 |
| 2 | Overall revision | 2.0 – 2.9 | Lacking 4-5 |
| 1 | No report | 1.0 – 1.9 | Lacking more than 5 |
B. Timeliness
| Rating | Submission |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | 3 days before deadline |
| 4 | 1-2 days before deadline |
| 3 | On the day |
| 2 | After deadline |
| 1 | No submission |
C. Efficiency
| Rating | % of Accomplishment |
| --- | --- |
| 5 | 95% above |
| 4 | 90%-94% |
| 3 | 80%-89% |
| 2 | 76%-79% |
| 1 | 75% and below |
3.9 The average rating of all employees within a department should not exceed that of the department head.
3.10 All DPCRs, UPCRs and IPCRs should include submission of the SALN, DTR, liquidation of cash advances and attendance in flag raising ceremonies.
3.11 The accomplishment of the University President, accomplishment of both faculty and personnel pursuant to CHED CMO No. 4 series of 2015

old_text:
4.1 For Light Offenses
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard/ Faculty/Personnel/ | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Student | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of the Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD. |
| Student | 3. Fills out a Permit to Enter the Campus/Attend Class if the offense is non-wearing of school ID because it was left at home or lost. |
| Student | 4. Fills out an Admission Slip if referred to the Office of the VPSD due to accumulated absences |
| Student | 5. Reports to the guidance counselor with the Disciplinary Action Slip with an attached promissory letter for the guidance counselor’s signature and admonition. |
| Guidance Counselor | 6. Gives admonition/Reminds student of the specific rule he/she Violated and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
| OSD Staff | 7. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Student | 8. Reports to the VPSD to clear his/her violation. |
| VPSD | 9. Evaluates the case, admonish the student, and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
4.2 For Serious and Very Serious Offenses:
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD |
| OSD Staff | 3. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Preliminary Hearing Committee (PHC) | 4. Determines if such a complaint or report is sufficient to warrant a formal investigation. In cases where the complaint or report is found sufficient, formal charges shall be filed and served upon the respondent and his/her parent or guardian. |
| Student Respondent | 5. Answers in writing within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the charges. If there is no reply, a formal investigation shall beheld. |
| Chair of the Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 6. Notifies the student as well as his/her parents/guardians regarding the date and venue of the formal hearing. |
| Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 7. Renders its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. |
| Student | 8. May appeal to the University President if the sanction is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, the appeal shall be elevated to the Board of Regents (BOR) for review. |
| University President | 9. Reviews the case and renders his/her decision if the decision is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, he/she elevates the case to the Board of Regents (BOR). |
| Board of Regents | 10. Reviews the decision of the SDC and renders final judgment. |

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)

3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.

Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)

Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

old_text:
The main objective of the LNU Strategic Performance Management System (SPMS) is directed towards a performance-oriented culture among its faculty and staff and to increase their understanding as to how their individual outputs count toward achieving the university MFOs and outcomes and in the process, help in achieving national outcomes as to its impact towards improving quality of lives, especially of the poor. Specifically, LNU SPMS will:
1.1 Align the university’s performance with the Philippine Development Plan which is results oriented, the university’s Strategic Plan, and the Organizational Performance Indicator Framework of the national government which focuses on strategic national and sectoral priorities in allocating scarce budgetary resources of the government and thus, make government officers/managers accountable for the strategies they develop and the outputs they are expected to deliver in pursuit of these priorities
1.2 Ensure the university’s effectiveness by cascading institutional accountabilities to the various levels within the university’s hierarchy especially in showing what outcomes the expenditure will produce
1.3 Link the LNU SPMS with other HR systems to ensure adherence to the principle of performance-based tenure adn incentives and rewards system
1.4 Foster continuous improvement of employee’s performance efficiency and productivity
1.5 Record attendance of workers for government regulations and laws
1.6 Provide data for payroll making purposes

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. Teh responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers

0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.3.4 Availability/Capacity (10%)
0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company

2 – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1.1 Accreditation of new external providers is necessary if existing external providers cannot meet the standard.
3.1.2 A List of Accredited External Providers shall be prepared and updated regularly.
3.1.3 Accreditation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.3.1 Quality of Product/Service based on product sample, demonstration or brochures (10%)
0 – three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
1 – one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
2 – meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.3.2 Price of products offered (70%)
0 – offers the highest price among the external providers
1 – offers a competitive or relatively lower price than the other external providers
2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers
3.1.3.3 Delivery Lead Time (10%)
0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.3.4 Availability/Capacity (10%)
0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
1 – can supply the average requirements of the company
2 – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

3.2.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.2.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria: 3.2.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (10%)
0 – three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
1 – one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
2 – meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.2.2.2 Price of products offered (70%)
0 – offers the highest price among the external providers
1 – offers a competitive or relatively lower price than the other external providers
2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers
3.2.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (10%)
0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, adn 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.

3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

old_text:
3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company
10-15 pts – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

| REGULAR | 75-100 | 50-74 | 15-49 | 0-14 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | Retain supplier | Retain supplier, point out weakness | Discretion of ED/CD | Suspend business |
| NEW | 30-50 | 20-29 | 10-19 | 0-9 |
| | Can start business | Can start business, ask to improve | Discretion of ED/CD | No business |

3.14.1 The University adheres to Section 5, Rule XVII of the Omnibus Rules Implementing Book V of Executive Order No. 292, all government officials and employees are required to render eight working hours a day for five days a week, or a total of 40 hours a week excluding time for lunch. The normal working hours shall be from 8 AM to 12 NN, and 1 PM to 5PM.
3.14.2 The University adheres to Section 6 of the same Rule allows the adoption of flexible working hours or ‘flexi-time’. CSC Memorandum Circular No. 14, s. 1989 prescribed that the flexi-time should not start earlier than 7 AM and not end later than 7 PM. In no case shall the flexi-time arrangement be occasionally changed by the employee at his or her convenience.
3.14.3 Those who fail to observe the eight-hour workday through consistent tardiness, undertime, and loafing from duty during office hours may be administratively charged and penalized with suspension or dismissal from service pursuant to civil service law, rules, and regulation.
3.14.4 The university is adopting mechanisms to strictly monitor and record attendance of employees by use of biometric time clocks system.

3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with the Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 The system of rewards and recognition shall be designed to encourage creativity, innovativeness, efficiency, integrity and productivity in the public service by recognizing and rewarding officials and employees individually or in groups for their suggestions, inventions, superior accomplishments and other personal efforts which contribute to the efficiency, economy or other improvement in government operations, or for other extraordinary acts or services in the public interest.
3.3 The Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) shall adhere to the principle of providing incentives and awards based on performance, innovative ideas and exemplary behavior.
3.4 The PRAISE shall provide both monetary and non-monetary awards and incentives to recognize, acknowledge and reward productive, creative, innovative and ethical behavior of employees through formal and informal mode.
3.5 A portion of the Human Resource Office funds shall be allocated for the PRAISE and incorporated in the LNU Annual Work and Financial Plan and Budget.

old_text:
3.1.1 Accreditation of new external providers is necessary if existing external providers cannot meet the standard.
3.1.2 A List of Accredited External Providers shall be prepared and updated regularly.
3.1.3 Accreditation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.3.1 Quality of Product/Service based on product sample, demonstration or brochures (10%)
0 – three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
1 – one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
2 – meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.3.2 Price of products offered (70%)
0 – offers the highest price among the external providers
1 – offers a competitive or relatively lower price than the other external providers
2 – offers the lowest price among the external providers
3.1.3.3 Delivery Lead Time (10%)
0 – has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
1 – has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to teh other external providers
2 – has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.3.4 Availability/Capacity (10%)
0 – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
1 – can supply the average requirements of the company
2 – can supply the maximum requirements of the company

3.1 Any records which may contain personal information shall be handled in accordance with the Republic Act 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.2 The system of rewards and recognition shall be designed to encourage creativity, innovativeness, efficiency, integrity and productivity in the public service by recognizing and rewarding officials and employees individually or in groups for their suggestions, inventions, superior accomplishments and other personal efforts which contribute to the efficiency, economy or other improvement in government operations, or for other extraordinary acts or services in the public interest.
3.3 The Program on Awards and Incentives for Service Excellence (PRAISE) shall adhere to the principle of providing incentives and awards based on performance, innovative ideas and exemplary behavior.
3.4 The PRAISE shall provide both monetary and non-monetary awards and incentives to recognize, acknowledge and reward productive, creative, innovative and ethical behavior of employees through formal and informal mode.
3.5 A portion of the Human Resource Office funds shall be allocated for the PRAISE and incorporated in the LNU Annual Work and Financial Plan and Budget.

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

3.1.1 External providers shall be evaluated based on their ability to meet company requirements. Evaluation of accredited external providers shall be done at least once a year.
3.1.2 Evaluation of external providers shall be based on the following criteria:
3.1.2.1 Quality of Product/Service (25 points maximum) – only for Regular External Providers
0-14 pts - three (3) or more deliveries/deliverables were rejected
15-19 pts - one (1) or two (2) deliveries/deliverables were rejected
20-25 pts - meets and exceeds the requirements of the requesting party
3.1.2.2 Price of products offered (35 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-9 pts - offers the highest price (10% more) among the external providers
10-24 pts - offers a competitive or relatively lower price (±10%) than the other external providers
25-35 pts - offers the lowest price (10% less) among the external providers
3.1.2.3 Delivery Lead Time (25 points maximum) - only for Regular External Providers
0-9 pts - has the longest delivery lead time among the external providers
10-19 pts - has a relatively shorter delivery lead time compared to the other external providers
20-25 pts - has the shortest delivery lead time among the external providers
3.1.2.4 Availability/Capacity (15 points maximum) – for both Regular and New External Providers
0-4 pts – cannot supply the average requirements of the company
5-9 pts – can supply the average requirements of the company

old_text:
3.1 It is the declared policy of the State that all resources of the government shall be managed, expended or utilized in accordance with laws and regulations, and safeguarded against loss or wastage through illegal or improper disposition, with a view to ensuring efficiency, economy and effectiveness in the operations of government. The responsibility to take care that such policy is faithfully adhered to rests directly with the chief or head of the government agency concerned. (Sec. 2, P.D. No. 1445)
3.2 No money shall be paid out of any public treasury or depository except in pursuance of an appropriation law or other specific statutory authority.
3.3 All laws and regulations applicable to financial transactions shall be faithfully adhered to.
3.4 No obligation shall be certified to accounts payable unless the obligation is founded on a valid claim that is properly supported by sufficient evidence and unless there is proper authority for its incurrence. Any certification for a non-existent or fictitious obligation and/or creditor shall be considered void. The certifying official shall be dismissed from the service, without prejudice to criminal prosecution under the provisions of the Revised Penal Code. Any payment made under such certification shall be illegal and every official authorizing or making such payment, or taking part therein or receiving such payment, shall be jointly and severally liable to government for the full amount so paid or received. (Book VI, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
3.5 The University President shall not incur nor authorize the incurrence of expenditures or obligations in excess of allotments released by the DBM Secretary for their respective departments, offices and agencies. Parties responsible for the incurrence of overdrafts shall be held personally liable therefor. (Book VI, Chapter 5, Section 41 of EO No. 292)
Any record, which may contain personal information, shall be handled in accordance with R.A. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
3.6 Any request for information shall be governed by E.O. No. 2, series of 2016 or the Freedom of Information Policy

4.1 For Light Offenses
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard/ Faculty/Personnel/ | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Student | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of the Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD. |
| Student | 3. Fills out a Permit to Enter the Campus/Attend Class if the offense is non-wearing of school ID because it was left at home or lost. |
| Student | 4. Fills out an Admission Slip if referred to the Office of the VPSD due to accumulated absences |
| Student | 5. Reports to the guidance counselor with the Disciplinary Action Slip with an attached promissory letter for the guidance counselor’s signature and admonition. |
| Guidance Counselor | 6. Gives admonition/Reminds student of the specific rule he/she Violated and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
| OSD Staff | 7. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Student | 8. Reports to the VPSD to clear his/her violation. |
| VPSD | 9. Evaluates the case, admonish the student, and signs the Student Violation Clearance Form, which is part of the Disciplinary Action Slip. |
4.2 For Serious and Very Serious Offenses:
| Responsibility | Activity |
| --- | --- |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 1. Issues two (2) copies of the Disciplinary Action Slip to the erring student. |
| Security Guard, Faculty/Staff | 2. Fills out one (1) copy of Disciplinary Referral Slip and submits it to the Office of the VPSD |
| OSD Staff | 3. Enters the case in the Student Violation Logbook. |
| Preliminary Hearing Committee (PHC) | 4. Determines if such a complaint or report is sufficient to warrant a formal investigation. In cases where the complaint or report is found sufficient, formal charges shall be filed and served upon the respondent and his/her parent or guardian. |
| Student Respondent | 5. Answers in writing within ten (10) calendar days from receipt of the charges. If there is no reply, a formal investigation shall beheld. |
| Chair of the Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 6. Notifies the student as well as his/her parents/guardians regarding the date and venue of the formal hearing. |
| Student Disciplinary Committee (SDC) | 7. Renders its decision by majority vote within fifteen days after it receives the complaint. |
| Student | 8. May appeal to the University President if the sanction is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, the appeal shall be elevated to the Board of Regents (BOR) for review. |
| University President | 9. Reviews the case and renders his/her decision if the decision is not more than five (5) days suspension, otherwise, he/she elevates the case to the Board of Regents (BOR). |
| Board of Regents | 10. Reviews the decision of the SDC and renders final judgment. |
